subject: Re: Unexpected mid-cycle usage surge — attribution & proposed credit
messages:
From: Leah Harper <leah.harper@brightcart.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected billing surge on Nov 30 invoice

Hi Alex / Ben,

We just received the Nov 30 invoice (attached) and there is a $87,400 overage line compared to our expected run-rate. Our engineering team did not push any production batch that would explain a ~30% token increase. Can you provide a per-service token breakdown and evidence of which envs and API keys generated the spike?

Specifically: 
- A time-series of daily tokens (2026-11-24 -> 2026-12-01) per API key
- Any large streaming sessions or bulk batch jobs between 11/28–11/30
- Whether requests from staging/test keys were excluded from billing

We need the breakdown for our accounts payable team and to decide whether to withhold the overage while we reconcile. Attaching the invoice (invoice_20261130.pdf).

Attachments: invoice_20261130.pdf (PDF, 220KB)

Thanks,
Leah Harper

Hi Leah — thanks for the flag and the invoice. Sorry for the stress here. I'm looping in Karthik from our billing instrumentation team to pull the packet-level attribution and usage export.

Ben and Karthik: can you grab a per-key daily token export for 2026-11-24 through 2026-12-01 and highlight any anomalous session lengths or duplicated request ids? BrightCart is asking whether staging/test traffic was billed; please also filter by env tag and return a list of keys with env=staging/test.

Leah — we'll aim to have the export and an initial root-cause hypothesis by EOD Monday PST. If it helps finance, we can also propose a provisional credit while we complete the audit.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Leah Harper <leah.harper@brightcart.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing surge on Nov 30 invoice

Hi Leah / Alex / Ben,

I pulled the per-key export and sliced by env tag, API key, and request_id. Short summary up top:
- Root cause: duplicate attribution introduced by a tenant-migration change in our ingress gateway. During a routing fallback deployed 2026-11-27, two upstream proxies set different client-id headers for the same requests; our dedupe key was only using request_id when present and fell back to the upstream client-id in a way that allowed duplicate attribution across two API keys for the same logical session.
- Impact: ~14% of tokens in the 11/28–11/30 window were double-counted (primary dataset: 2026-11-28T00:00 -> 2026-12-01T00:00). That maps to the ~$12.3k of the overage on invoice_20261130.pdf.
- Scope: Affected keys: bc-prod-01, bc-prod-02, bc-batch-ingest-key. No evidence staging/test env tags were billed (staging keys show <0.1% of the spike).

I attached the usage export (filtered view) and a small example of duplicated request events for one session (rows 1217–1225 show identical request_id with two distinct client-id headers). We also captured the gateway change logs (internal) showing the fallback rule that activated at 2026-11-27T03:14:22Z.

Proposed remediation:
1) Apply retroactive de-duplication for the affected window and issue a credit of $12,340 against invoice_20261130.
2) Patch the ingress dedupe logic to prefer canonical request_id + tenant_id and add an automated regression test.
3) Share an audit package (filtered usage export + internal gateway logs) for BrightCart finance.

If you confirm step (1) we can raise the credit memo and apply it to your account; we'd also provide a signed PDF of the audit evidence for your records.

Attachments: usage_export_20261201.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Billing Instrumentation
Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Leah Harper <leah.harper@brightcart.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: finance@brightcart.com
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected billing surge on Nov 30 invoice

Thanks Karthik — that explanation aligns with what our eng saw when spot-checking request samples. We accept the proposed remediation and credit of $12,340.

Two asks from finance before we close the loop: 
1) Please provide a short signed audit package (CSV + gateway logs + brief cover note) we can attach to the GL. A PDF with a Redwood engineer signature is preferred.
2) Please generate a credit memo (DocuSign link preferred) referencing invoice_20261130 and DC-34821; our AP team will route it for payment processing.

If you can start the DocuSign flow and upload the audit PDF to the Drive link you shared, we'll confirm receipt and release the remaining balance.

Leah
Head of Platform Ops, BrightCart
Attachments: none
